solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give back proceeds

definitions.meaning: to give back something is to hand it over to its owner again
the proceeds of a venture are the money or profit it yields

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a verb meaning restore, and a noun for the yield or profit on an investment.

clue.text: See Eric with iPod shuffle every now and then

indicators.note: an iPod shuffle is a music player, but here shuffle tells us to mix up the letters of the two names

explanation.surface: Someone catches sight of Eric listening to his iPod Shuffle from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffle' rearranges ERIC and IPOD together; 'See' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something periodic happens at intervals, recurring every so often rather than constantly.

clue.text: Reversal of fortune follows winning team getting in disarray

indicators.note: follows puts the reversal piece after the winning-team pieces

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead, winning the contest
a side is a sports team
a downturn or down is a setback, a reversal of fortune

explanation.surface: After leading, a team suffers a turn of luck and falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversal of fortune' looks like the definition, but 'follows' places it last; 'getting' links to the real definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Things turned upside down are in a chaotic mess, an idiomatic picture of total disorder.

clue.text: Solemn, missing good party

indicators.note: missing says a piece is absent, so the abbreviation for good is taken out of the synonym

parts.note: grave means solemn or serious

explanation.surface: A serious-minded person, lacking cheer, misses out on a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively party, typically with dance music, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Firm supporting one's request — don't mention it!

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes last

parts.note: my stands for one's, the speaker's own
a plea is an earnest request
sure means firm or steady, as in a sure footing

explanation.surface: A company backs up someone's appeal, then tells them not to speak of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but means SURE, placed under MY PLEA by 'supporting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are polite replies to thanks, conversational equivalents saying the favour was no trouble.

clue.text: French policeman: not quite The Pink Panther?

indicators.note: not quite tells us to stop short of the full word, losing its final letter

parts.note: The Pink Panther is a film, colloquially a flick

explanation.surface: Is Inspector Clouseau of the Pink Panther films not quite a proper French policeman?
explanation.walkthrough: The film has a French policeman in it, which tempts solvers to look for Clouseau; instead the film itself is a FLICK, cut short by 'not quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flic is French slang for a police officer, much as cop is in English.

clue.text: Drag disrupting most of support for highly prized fish

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into another word, so one piece is placed inside the other
most of drops the last letter of the word for support

parts.note: to bear is to support or carry
to lug is to drag something heavy

explanation.surface: Dragging a heavy load interferes with the supports for a much-valued fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the support word to BEA before 'disrupting' breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a sturgeon whose roe is the most prized caviar, so the fish is highly valued.

clue.text: Passionate macho types held in check

indicators.note: held in means the macho types are placed inside the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine carefully
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: Fiery tough guys are being kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and intense in feeling, a close synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Politician in early spinning after letter giving warning

indicators.note: after puts the spun piece behind the letter

parts.note: ex is the spelt-out name of the letter X

indicators.note: in puts the politician inside the scrambled letters
spinning means the letters of early are whirled round into a new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP spins early after receiving a letter of warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges EARLY to ELARY, with MP inserted to give EMPLARY; the name of the letter X goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplary punishment serves as a warning or deterrent to others, an established sense of the word.

clue.text: Subject, for example found in press

indicators.note: found in means the abbreviation sits inside the word for press

parts.note: to lie heavily on something is to press on it

explanation.surface: A news subject, for instance, turns up in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalism but is the verb, as in weighing down; 'found in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a liege man was a vassal, a subject owing allegiance to a lord.

clue.text: Tune is oddly catching — I could make single

indicators.note: catching means the anagram takes the next letter inside it
oddly signals that the letters of tune is are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A catchy tune, oddly enough, makes the speaker feel single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges the first two words into UNTISE, and 'catching' takes the I in after the N; 'could' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unitise is to form into one unit, combining parts into a single whole.

clue.text: Authoritative discourse from English court stopping enticement

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces go inside the word for enticement

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or bait

explanation.surface: A weighty speech is given by an English court cracking down on temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture is a formal talk by an expert, so authoritative discourse describes it well.

clue.text: Drop off fellow on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read in the return direction

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man falls asleep while heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep, and to nod or nod off means the same.

clue.text: More work in recession with most recent forecast

parts.note: extra means more, additional

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the word for work is read in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
late can mean most recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: Economists predict more work in a downturn according to the latest figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns the work abbreviation round, a nod to the economic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project known trends forward, inferring or predicting future values.

clue.text: Financial authorities in attempts to conceal a sure upset

indicators.note: to conceal means the attempts wrap round the other letters, hiding them inside

parts.note: tries are attempts

indicators.note: upset means the letters of a sure are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Finance departments try to hide a sure-fire disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the two words into EASUR, which 'to conceal' hides inside the attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasuries are government departments managing public money, such as the UK Treasury.

clue.text: Stoics prepared to admit sect who believe in the supernatural

indicators.note: to admit means letting something in, so the anagram takes the sect inside
prepared means made ready in a new form, so the letters of stoics are rearranged

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: Philosophers are ready to let a sect join those who believe in the supernatural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the philosophers into OCISTS, and 'to admit' lets the sect in.
explanation.definitionFit: Occultists practise or believe in the occult, magical and supernatural forces.

clue.text: Chocolate and cocoa are obtained originally here

definitions.text: Chocolate and cocoa are obtained originally here

indicators.note: originally points to the beginnings, the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: This is the source from which chocolate and cocoa both come.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words before 'originally' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao tree bears the beans from which chocolate and cocoa are made.

clue.text: Only women subordinate to important person in organisation get nickname

indicators.note: subordinate means placed below, so in this down entry it comes second

parts.note: a cog is a part essential to a machine or organisation
a group of only women has no men

explanation.surface: In a firm, women-only staff work under a big boss and get a nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only women' gives NO MEN; 'get' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a name or nickname, originally the third name of a Roman citizen.

clue.text: Object as wings are cut in bird

indicators.note: wings are cut means both outer letters are clipped off

parts.note: to demur is to object

explanation.surface: Someone protests as a bird's wings are clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Trainee accountant finds liability having third concealed

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: having third concealed means the third letter of the word is hidden away

parts.note: a debt is a liability

explanation.surface: A junior accountant finds a debt with part of it hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having third concealed' removes the third letter, B, from DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young trainee, especially in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Admit car crash to be spectacular

indicators.note: crash means smashed up, so the letters of admit car are jumbled

explanation.surface: Owning up to a car crash makes for a big scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges ADMIT CAR; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is striking and spectacular, as a stage drama aims to be.

clue.text: Shift in public opinion as government turns fortunate

parts.note: rounds are turns, as in a game
well can mean fortunate, as in it is well that we came

explanation.surface: Public mood changes as the government turns out lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a growing tide of feeling among the public, likened to a deep ocean swell.

clue.text: Type of band against backing celebrity

parts.note: on can mean against, as leaning on a wall

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for celebrity is reversed

parts.note: a name is a famous person, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A band type opposes support for a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the celebrity word round to EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band is a street performer playing several instruments at once.

clue.text: Melody regularly coming from aviary

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A tune is heard repeatedly from a birdhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, as in a Londonderry air.

clue.text: Blemish in image eradicated, initially in further tint

indicators.note: in places the initial letter inside the word for further tint

parts.note: to redye is to tint again

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of eradicated

explanation.surface: A flaw in a picture is removed first, then the colour is touched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'further tint' means dye again; 'in' drops the first letter of 'eradicated' into the middle of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the red glare in pupils caused by flash photography, a common photo flaw.

clue.text: Performing in opera — as at Verona?

indicators.note: performing means putting on an act, so the letters of in opera are presented in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Singers appear in an opera, like those staged at Verona.
explanation.walkthrough: The Verona Arena stages famous outdoor opera seasons, so the definition is by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera at Verona is staged in a Roman arena with no roof, an outdoor setting.

clue.text: Depositor, after initial loss, makes claim

indicators.note: after initial loss means once the first letter is lost

parts.note: a saver deposits money in a bank

explanation.surface: A bank customer who lost money files a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert firmly, to claim something as true.

clue.text: Outlaw swindle introduced by gang

indicators.note: introduced by means brought inside, so the swindle goes within the gang word

parts.note: a band is a gang
to rig is to fix or swindle

explanation.surface: A gang brings in a crooked scheme for a bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, an outlaw who robs travellers.

clue.text: Raised money for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds raised are checked by an auditor.
explanation.walkthrough: An auditor sounds like an accountant here, but is a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or children bred are raised, reared up.

clue.text: Cheer as long drink knocked back followed by a short one

indicators.note: followed by puts the next piece after
knocked back means turned backwards, also a nod to drinking

parts.note: ale is a long drink, served by the pint

indicators.note: short means cut, losing the last letter

parts.note: one refers to another drink, here tea

explanation.surface: A toast as one beer goes down and then a small chaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses ALE to ELA; the second drink, tea, is 'short' its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with joy, to cheer someone up.

clue.text: Shock as unknown tree from the east gets chosen first

indicators.note: first puts this piece at the start

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect

indicators.note: from the east means reading right to left in an across entry

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
a fir is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree from the east is a shock to whoever is selected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses Y FIR to RIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify is to thrill or startle, as if delivering an electric shock.
